source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: AI token demand is at extreme early innings — fewer than 10 million true heavy-paying users out of 1.5 billion knowledge workers; supply is massively constrained relative to addressable demand
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI token demand is in the extreme early innings, with fewer than 10 million genuine heavy-paying users out of a potential 1.5 billion knowledge workers — meaning the market is barely 1% penetrated on the demand side. He supports this with granular internal and portfolio data: Atreides' own token consumption grew 100x from March to August 2026, AI-native a16z portfolio companies spend 10%+ of human compensation on tokens versus ~1% for old-economy leaders, and a single enterprise tool like Grockbot could 10-20x a company's token spend in one month. The power-law dynamic within enterprises — where top engineers consume 10-100x the median — means aggregate demand will compound far faster than linear adoption curves suggest. The investment implication is that compute supply is massively constrained relative to addressable demand, making infrastructure providers (particularly GPU and data center capacity) the clearest near-term beneficiaries, while the thesis is explicitly not winner-take-all at the frontier-lab layer.
detail: Baker estimates fewer than 10M genuine heavy token consumers (taking the under on 30M). Power law within enterprises: highest-spending engineers use 10-100x median. AI-native a16z portfolio companies spend 10%+ of human compensation on tokens; old-economy leaders spend ~1%. Atreides internal token consumption up 100x from March to August 2026. Grockbot Enterprise access may 10-20x their spend in a single month.
confidence_evidence: Baker uses his own firm's data (100x token growth) and portfolio company data as primary evidence; speaks with high conviction
